text:
Predicates:
DesignStyle(x) ::: x is a design style.
Admires(x, y) ::: x admires y.
InterestingGeometries(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
Brutalist(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
ZahaStyle(x) ::: x is a style of Zaha Hadid.
KellyStyle(x) ::: x is a style of Kelly Wearstler.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
DesignBy(x, y) ::: x is a design by y.
StyleOf(x, y) ::: x is the style of y.
Design(x) ::: x is a design.
Max(x) ::: x is Max.
Premises:
∀x (DesignStyle(x) ∧ Admires(Max, x) → InterestingGeometries(x)) ::: All styles Max adores that are design styles have interesting geometries.
∀x (Admires(Max, x) ∧ StyleOf(x, y) ∧ Brute(y) → ¬InterestingGeometries(x)) ::: No adored style that is a brutalist style has interesting geometries.
∀x (Admires(Max, x) → (ZahaStyle(x) ∨ KellyStyle(x))) ::: Every style Max adores is either Zaha Hadid's or Kelly Wearstler's.
∀x (KellyStyle(x) ∧ Admires(Max, x) → Evocative(x)) ::: All Kelly Wearstler styles Max adores are evocative.
∀x (KellyStyle(x) ∧ Admires(Max, x) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All Kelly Wearstler styles Max adores are dreamy.
∀x ((DesignBy(x, y) ∧ Admires(Max, x) ∧ InterestingGeometries(x)) → (Brutalist(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If a Max design he adores has interesting geometries, then it is a brutalist building and evocative.
Conclusion:
DesignBy(z, max) ∧ Brutalist(z) ::: A design by Max is a brutalist building.
